title: Contes de Perrault
author: Charles Perrault
blurb: Eight classic fairy tales, including Little Red Riding Hood, Cinderella and Sleeping Beauty, in short, clear sentences.
note: Written in 1697 by an author who died in 1703, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Gustave Doré, Little Red Riding Hood in bed with the wolf, for Les Contes de Perrault, 1862. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: La Parure
author: Guy de Maupassant
blurb: A woman borrows a diamond necklace for one evening and loses it. A short story with a famous ending.
note: Published in 1884 and the author died in 1893, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir, La Loge (The Theater Box), 1874. The Courtauld, London. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Le Horla
author: Guy de Maupassant
blurb: A diary of a man who becomes convinced that an invisible being has moved into his house.
note: Published in 1887 and the author died in 1893, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Odilon Redon, Eye-Balloon, 1878. Museum of Modern Art, New York. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Candide, ou l’Optimisme
author: Voltaire
blurb: A naive young man is thrown out of paradise and told that everything is for the best, while disaster follows him around the world.
note: Published in 1759 by an author who died in 1778, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Jean-Honoré Fragonard, The Swing, 1767. The Wallace Collection, London. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Lettres de mon moulin
author: Alphonse Daudet
blurb: Short sketches of Provence written from an old windmill: shepherds, priests, smugglers and a goat who wants to be free.
note: Published in 1869 and the author died in 1897, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Vincent van Gogh, Harvest in Provence, 1888. Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Le Tour du monde en quatre-vingts jours
author: Jules Verne
blurb: Phileas Fogg bets that he can circle the globe in eighty days, with his servant Passepartout and a detective on his trail.
note: Published in 1872 to 1873 and the author died in 1905, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: J. M. W. Turner, Rain, Steam and Speed: The Great Western Railway, 1844. National Gallery, London. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Madame Bovary
author: Gustave Flaubert
blurb: The wife of a country doctor looks for a more exciting life in affairs and debt.
note: Published in 1857 and the author died in 1880, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Albert-Auguste Fourié, The Death of Madame Bovary, 1883. Musée des Beaux-Arts de Rouen. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
